parsed.notes: Lens B only; no support, pincite, or quote-fidelity defect is raised.

reasons: Lake identity is verified and matches Gouled v. United States, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1921-02-28.
Lake citations include official 255 U.S. 298, parallel cites 41 S. Ct. 261 and 65 L. Ed. 647, and vendor-neutral 1921 U.S. LEXIS 1826.
Nothing in the disclosed record disproves the authority's existence; later negative treatment is addressed separately.
residual_risks: Currentness after the disclosed as-of-treatment date, 2026-06-30, is not independently verifiable from these files.

reasons: Lens B does not attack support placement except for currency/treatment implications.
The Historical (foil) role is consistent with the page's Historical label and the lake treatment field_i_validity of superseded.
The disclosed scope note says the mere-evidence rule was overruled/abandoned while a separate Gouled principle retains vitality, which fits a historical-foil treatment role.
residual_risks: No independent review of the Trespass home-page taxonomy is available in the disclosed files.

reasons: Lens B does not raise quote or holding-support defects.
The holding expressly says the mere-evidence rule was overruled by Warden v. Hayden, matching the lake scope note's overruled/abandoned treatment.
The surviving ruse-entry formulation matches the lake scope note's statement that the separate stealth/ruse/social-pretext holding retains vitality.
residual_risks: The disclosed negative edges are point-null, so the file does not independently map every later treatment event to each Gouled sub-rule.

defect.evidence_quote: The mere-evidence rule was overruled/abandoned by Warden v. Hayden (1967), which held the Fourth Amendment does not bar the seizure of items of solely evidentiary value. The separate Gouled holding — that entry obtained by stealth, ruse, or social pretext can render a subsequent search unreasonable — retains vitality.
defect.problem: The standalone authority_weight label 'Binding — SCOTUS' is overbroad unless it is explicitly only a court-hierarchy label; the disclosed treatment says Gouled is superseded/overruled in part and only a separate point retains vitality.
defect.proposed_fix: Render as 'SCOTUS; superseded/overruled in part' or rename this field to court_weight and always display it with the treatment status.

reasons: The lake identity supports SCOTUS hierarchy, but the treatment fields prevent an unqualified current-law binding label.
A user or filter consuming only authority_weight could treat the overruled mere-evidence rule as binding.
residual_risks: If the corpus defines authority_weight strictly as court hierarchy, the value is internally defensible but should not be shown without treatment.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Disambiguate court weight from current precedential validity.

defect.evidence_quote: The mere-evidence rule was overruled/abandoned by Warden v. Hayden (1967), which held the Fourth Amendment does not bar the seizure of items of solely evidentiary value. The separate Gouled holding — that entry obtained by stealth, ruse, or social pretext can render a subsequent search unreasonable — retains vitality.
defect.problem: The core superseded/overruled-in-part treatment stands, but varies_by_point=false is inconsistent with the disclosed scope note distinguishing an overruled mere-evidence rule from a surviving stealth/ruse-entry principle.
defect.proposed_fix: Set varies_by_point=true and add point_overrides for the mere-evidence rule as superseded/overruled by Warden v. Hayden and the stealth/ruse-entry principle as retained/good to that extent.

reasons: Lake field_i_validity=superseded and the Warden negative edge support the principal negative treatment call.
The same disclosed treatment note expressly separates the overruled mere-evidence point from the retained ruse-entry point, so the no-variation flag should not stand unmodified.
The content page also describes the status as overruled in part and identifies a surviving principle.
residual_risks: No disclosed evidence after 2026-06-30 is available.
The lake negative-treatment edges are largely point-null, so precise point mapping should be encoded rather than inferred at render time.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Align the display label 'overruled' with the frontmatter value 'superseded' or document the mapping between those labels.
